recent_posts.title: Early and late-stage hypergrowth.
recent_posts.summary: A reflection on the distinction between early-stage and late-stage hypergrowth and how it affects leadership decisions. In early-stage hypergrowth, companies serially solve their biggest problems, making it sensible to expand existing leaders' scope. In late-stage hypergrowth, companies must solve everything simultaneously to satisfy a skeptical late majority, making that approach counterproductive. The author draws a parallel to the current AI era, noting that small AI-empowered teams can speedrun early hypergrowth but it remains unclear whether the same approach works for late-stage hypergrowth — pointing to challenges like Anthropic's messaging to Claude Code power users as symptoms of this transition.

recent_posts.title: Agents as scaffolding for recurring tasks.
recent_posts.summary: A practical pattern for building reliable agent-based automation: start with a fully agent-driven prototype to understand the problem, then refactor to a hybrid where deterministic code handles flow control and filtering, while agents are narrowly scoped to tasks requiring judgment (like identifying code owners). Illustrated with a real Dependabot security alert workflow that failed when agents were used as drop-in software replacements but succeeded once code handled severity filtering and agents only resolved ownership ambiguity. The result is faster, cheaper, and more maintainable automation.

recent_posts.title: The agentic passive voice.
recent_posts.summary: A short satirical piece coining the term 'agentic passive voice' to call out developers who blame AI models (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) for mistakes instead of taking personal responsibility. The author argues that attributing errors to AI tools is a form of deflection, and urges engineers to write — and think — in the active voice, owning the outcomes of their AI-assisted work.

recent_posts.title: How coding agents shift the bottleneck from implementation to judgment
recent_posts.summary: A reflection on how coding agents are transforming software development, using two real-world infrastructure migrations as a lens: one at Uber in 2014 and one at Imprint in 2026. The key insight is that coding agents have largely solved the constraints of time and attention, shifting the primary bottleneck to judgment — knowing how to build software that is maintainable, secure, and reliable. The author proposes that 'datapacks' or skill packages (expert context injected into coding agents) will scale judgment, and that creativity will be the final frontier after judgment is addressed.

recent_posts.title: Refactoring internal documentation in Notion
recent_posts.summary: A practical guide to cleaning up organizational documentation in Notion after migrating from Confluence. The approach involved diagnosing key issues (stale content, duplication, unclear ownership), establishing clear policies (optimize for AI search, eliminate duplication, prefer version-controlled docs), and implementing automated solutions. Custom scripts were built to archive 1,500+ expired pages, identify buried current content in stale hierarchies, detect broken links, and validate key documentation. The entire effort took approximately 8 hours and required no additional team resources.

recent_posts.title: Should you include engineers in your leadership meetings?
recent_posts.summary: Including senior engineers directly in leadership meetings creates better decision-making by keeping leaders grounded in technical reality. The approach involves having senior engineers report directly to the Head of Engineering/CTO and participate fully in leadership discussions alongside managers. Benefits include preventing management from becoming disconnected from actual work, enabling faster technical decisions, creating alternative information channels, and setting expectations that managers stay technical while engineers understand management. The main filter is that it exposes engineers who want authority without accountability.

recent_posts.title: Writing Visualizations with Remotion
recent_posts.summary: Remotion combined with Claude Code integration enables rapid creation of data visualizations. The author created multiple videos visualizing blog post data (publication timeline, tag frequency, posts per employer) in under 10 minutes using Claude prompts to generate datasets and visuals. The experience demonstrated how effectively AI-assisted tools can generate complex video visualizations with minimal effort.

recent_posts.title: Curiosity is the first-step in problem solving.
recent_posts.summary: Leading with curiosity before jumping to solutions reduces the cost of being wrong in ambiguous situations. When facing hiring decisions, incident responses, or technical disagreements, asking questions and seeking to understand context prevents damaging relationships through premature accountability. The approach involves explicitly sharing mental models, asking where others agree or disagree, and building systems that automate curiosity-driven responses. This mindset acknowledges that many senior-level problems lack complete information, making it more valuable to make mistakes cheaply than to avoid them entirely.

recent_posts.title: Stripe's Lighthouse Hiring pattern.
recent_posts.summary: Lighthouse Hiring is a strategic recruiting pattern where companies hire well-connected individuals to improve both the quality and velocity of subsequent hires. The approach worked exceptionally well at Stripe, with examples like Julia Evans, Avi Bryant, and Raylene Yung serving as connection points for numerous high-quality hires. However, it requires careful management of power dynamics and role design to avoid internal bias perceptions and dependency risks.

recent_posts.title: Why applying pressure without a plan creates chaos in engineering teams
recent_posts.summary: Applying pressure to teams without a clear execution plan creates chaos and leads to failure. The pattern appears in various contexts: failed product launches, poorly planned service migrations, and metrics-driven AI adoption initiatives. Effective leaders transform external pressure into actionable plans through iterative strategy refinement. The anti-pattern often stems from misapplied management by objectives, where executives set targets for low-agency teams without involving them in goal-setting or implementation planning.
